title: HumanChatV2 envelope
description:
The first-party human message envelope, carried as an opaque payload by a transport that stays payload-agnostic. It is an APPLICATION protocol and versions independently of transport v2. This schema describes the RAW (decompressed) JSON form; the `;ce=br` media-type parameter marks the same envelope brotli-compressed whole, decoded above transport under the 196,608-byte decompressed ceiling of ADR-0050 before this shape applies.

NOTE THE DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY WITH THE TRANSPORT SCHEMAS: this one does NOT set `additionalProperties: false`. HumanChatV2 specifies that unknown fields are ignored for forward compatibility within v2 bounds, so a receiver must accept an envelope carrying fields it has never heard of. Closing it here would turn a forward-compatible message into a validation failure and break the property the version number exists to provide. Where the transport schemas close the object to make an omission enforceable, this one is open because openness is the specified behaviour — the difference is intentional in both directions.

No field here can influence retention. There is no sender-controlled persistence field, and `from_endpoint`, `reply_to`, unknown extensions, or the text itself cannot request or force the receiver to keep anything (ADR-0044).

kind.description: The only v2 kind. Attachments, edits, reactions, typing indicators, delivery/read receipts, and multi-device sync are explicitly not part of HumanChatV2; artifact/attachment references await their own ADR (ADR-0050 rule 9).

app_message_id.description: Exactly 16 CSPRNG bytes as 32 LOWERCASE hex characters. Uppercase, prefixes, separators, and other lengths are invalid — a canonical form is what makes `reply_to` comparison exact. This is application reply/retention identity and is NOT the DirectMessageV2 dedup identity; the two live at different layers and must not be conflated.

text.description: UTF-8 markdown: CommonMark plus the table and strikethrough extensions, under the CLOSED subset of ADR-0050 — raw HTML renders as literal text, link schemes are allowlisted (https, mailto), remote images are never auto-fetched, block nesting <= 16 and tables <= 256x32 (bounds in clients/human/HUMAN-CHAT.md). A construct outside the subset falls back to plain-text display; it does not reject the envelope, so the subset is a RENDERING contract, not a shape constraint this schema could express. Bounded in practice by the transport payload ceiling (after compression when compression is used) rather than by a field limit here.

reply_to.description: Same canonical grammar. The referenced message NEED NOT exist locally: an unknown reference neither rejects the envelope nor triggers a network lookup, and the UI shows a neutral placeholder. Treating it as a fetchable pointer would turn a display hint into a remote-triggered request.

sent_at_ms.description: Display and diagnostics only — never trust, replay, freshness, or ordering authority. The ceiling is 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z; outside the closed interval is malformed. A receiver may suppress or annotate an implausible time without changing acceptance.

from_endpoint.description: AN UNAUTHENTICATED DISPLAY HINT. Direct transport metadata is authoritative for source_peer and the peer-asserted source_endpoint; a conflicting value here is ignored for routing and authority. On broadcast it is unauthenticated by construction, because transport broadcast origin is PeerId-only (ADR-0030) — so a UI that renders this as identity is asserting something the transport never verified.
